haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes from creation (expires_at = now + 10 min). The sweeper releases it every minute after expiry, and a late claim is refused.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge (I1 before O5). If any line is short, nothing is reserved or charged, and the order is REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK.
haiku-low.q3: The charge uses the order id as the provider idempotency key, and Payment stores one charge row per order id.
haiku-low.q4: The claim is refused, Payment refunds the full amount, Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and the customer is emailed. A partial order is never shipped.
haiku-low.q5: The cart is emptied by Cart when OrderConfirmed is handled, after a successful claim. On any failed checkout, the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service drives checkout steps. Its orders table holds the order status (for example PENDING_STOCK, AWAITING_PAYMENT), which records progress.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment verifies it, records the event id, and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined via its outbox to the broker, which Order handles.
haiku-low.q8: Each webhook event id is recorded once, and repeats are acknowledged and ignored. A charge also changes only from PENDING, so repeats cannot change it.
haiku-low.q9: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined. Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release the hold immediately, not waiting for the sweeper.
haiku-low.q10: The claim decides: if the hold is no longer HELD or has expired, the design refunds. It refunds in every late-success case, even if stock is still free.
haiku-low.q11: Payment retries with backoff using the same key (order id plus refund), up to a limit. Then it sets REFUND_FAILED and it goes to the ops queue. Refunds table tracks it.
haiku-low.q12: Receiving OrderConfirmed causes Cart to empty its lines. The Cart service does this, and does nothing if this order already emptied it.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes (expires_at = creation + 10 min). If not claimed in time, the sweeper (runs every minute) sets it RELEASED, returning stock to sale; a claim after expiry is refused.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging (charge is requested only after the hold exists). If any line is short, nothing is reserved (all-or-nothing transaction), Inventory returns 409 with the short items, order is REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, no payment requested, customer told which items are short.
sonnet.q3: Idempotency key: the order id is used as the provider's key, and Payment stores one charge row per order id, so a repeat is recognised and not acted on twice.
sonnet.q4: The claim is refused; Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, Payment refunds the full amount, and the customer is emailed. Money refunded in full; no partial order shipped.
sonnet.q5: Emptied only when OrderConfirmed is handled (Cart empties its lines). On every failure branch the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q6: The Order service drives the steps (it calls Cart, Inventory and Payment and reacts to events). The record of progress is the order's status stored in the Order service (PENDING_STOCK, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, etc.).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which verifies the signature, updates the charge, and publishes PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined as an event (via outbox and message broker); Order reacts to that event.
sonnet.q8: Each webhook's event id is recorded once; a repeat id is acknowledged with 200 and ignored. Also a charge changes only from PENDING, so a repeated outcome can't change it again.
sonnet.q9: The stock is released back to sale immediately (hold set to RELEASED). Triggered by Payment publishing PaymentDeclined, upon which Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release the hold, without waiting for the sweeper.
sonnet.q10: It does not decide: it always refunds in every late-success case (claim refused, order cancelled). The alternative of trying a fresh reservation and confirming is listed as an open decision to make before building.
sonnet.q11: Payment retries with backoff using the same key (so no double refund), recording each attempt. After the retry limit it sets REFUND_FAILED and the refund stays on the ops queue until refunded, never dropped. Tracked in Payment's refunds (status and attempt count) and the ops queue.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event (published by Order); the Cart service empties its lines (no-op if already emptied for that order).
